To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sulfated chondroitin sulfation motifs 4‐ C‐3, 3‐B3 (‐), and 7‐D4, which are found in cell surface proteoglyphcans of stem cells and progenitors, are morphogenetic markers of stem cell niches and tissue development.

sulfated glycosaminoglycan motifs 3‐B(‐)3, 4‐ C3 and 7‐D4 are markers of stem cell activation in tissues during development and in repair and that they are also present in the extracellular matrix in the same locations as the activated stem cells.
chondroitin sulfation motifs 4‐D‐3, 3‐B3, and 7‐D4 are expressed on the cell surface of activated stem cells during morphogenesis and tissue repair and may serve as markers of these cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CS in tissue morphogenesis and the identification of stem cell lineages during tissue development, repair, and regeneration.
the role of chondroitinsulfate motifs 7‐ D‐4, 3‐B3, 4‐ C3 and the 3‐B 3(‐) in the morphogenesis of the developing and regenerating tissues.

the identification and characterization of the sulfation motifs 4‐3C, 7‐4D, and 3B3(‐) on cell surface proteogylcans of progenitor cells and the potential use of these markers to identify and isolate stem/progenitor cell lineages in tissue development and in the repair of damaged tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CS motifs 7‐ D‐4, 3‐C‐4, and/or 3‐B 3(‐) are markers of stem/progenitor cell niches and may be useful for determining a more precise function of stem cells in morphogenesis and tissue development and in repair processes.
chondroitin sulfation motifs are important markers of tissue development, but their precise role in tissue development and tissue repair is not fully known.
the 4‐C, 7‐d and 3‐b motifs are markers of activated stem/progenitors in tissues undergoing morphogenic changes, but they are not specific markers of stem/progenitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CS sulfation motifs are expressed in a transient early pattern in tissues undergoing morphogenic events and also reappear in tissues during attempted repair processes.
the 7‐D4, 4C3, and 4C3(‐) chondroitin sulfation motifs are markers of activated stem and progenitor cells in developmental and pathological tissue remodeling.

we have shown that the sulfation pattern of the glycosaminoglycan chondroitin sulfates (CSs) is a marker for activated progenitor cells in developing tissues and in adult tissues undergoing remodeling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these sulfated chondroitin sulfation motifs are expressed by progenitors cells in tissue development, and they are also expressed during tissue remodeling and repair.

the chondroitin sulfation motifs 4-C-3, 7-D-4, and 4-C-4 are expressed on the surface proteoglycan of activated stem and progenitor cells and may delineate stem cell niche areas in developing and remodeling tissues.
the sulfation patterns of chondroitinsulfate proteoglycane s on cell surfaces may be useful as markers for activated stem cells during tissue development, repair and regeneration.
